comparison: Both evaluate the amino acid ratio findings (C82-C84, C11). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to smaller subsample, sensitivity to outliers (p=0.064 when extreme point removed), and exploratory nature. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing it as valuable evidence for dopamine-dependent mechanisms, though editor notes more direct dopamine measures would strengthen conclusions.

Both address mechanistic interpretations of genetic findings (C97-C98, C103-C108). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, stating interpretations are consistent with computational models and established literature. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing need for more direct dopamine measures to confirm mechanistic hypotheses and noting complexity of compensatory mechanisms.

Both evaluate DARPP-32 findings (C76-C79). OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence across two genetic markers strengthening conclusions. Peer reviewers confirm the genetic moderation pattern is consistent across both SNPs, noting stronger effects in G-carriers.

Both address main BMI effect on working memory (C57-C59). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate statistics and clear reporting despite contradicting hypothesis. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that it contradicts initial hypothesis and suggesting interpretation should emphasize genetic moderation effects as more informative than overall BMI effect.

Both address control variable findings (C60-C63). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as part of primary analysis showing main BMI effect. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED (implicit acceptance), viewing these as methodological validation showing task sensitivity to expected cognitive and demographic factors.

Both evaluate theoretical context for COMT null findings (C109-C112). OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citation of conflicting meta-analyses and explanation of why COMT might not show effects. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this framing without explicit challenge.

Both evaluate Taq1A genetic moderation findings (C64-C70). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing specificity to updating condition and appropriate statistical corrections. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, confirming this as a key result with visual inspection supporting selective genetic effects in updating condition.

Both address probe type analysis (C71-C75). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting this validates task design and shows genetic effects are robust across probe types. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED through implicit acceptance, not explicitly discussing but not challenging these methodological validation findings.

Both evaluate COMT and C957T null findings (C80-C81, C64-C66). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting clear reporting with appropriate statistics and theoretical justification. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about statistical power given small genetic effect sizes and BMI distribution, suggesting null findings may reflect insufficient power rather than true absence of effects.

Both address dual-mechanism interpretation (C6-C7, C9, C12, C99-C100). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, stating interpretation of both dopamine-dependent and dopamine-independent mechanisms is reasonable given data pattern. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting this interpretation and emphasizing importance of inter-individual variability and protective effects of advantageous genotypes.

Partial overlap on amino acid ratio measure (C10-C11, C116-C118). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting limitations of amino acid ratio as dopamine proxy and sensitivity to outliers. Peer reviewers (R5) rate findings as SUPPORTED but focus on behavioral results rather than validity of amino acid ratio as dopamine measure, with editor noting more direct measures would strengthen work.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive methodological details (C51-C56, C85-C96) as SUPPORTED, noting clear documentation of sample characteristics, task design, ethical approvals, and pre-registration. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological reporting claims.

OpenEval evaluates theoretical framework claims about working memory gating and dopamine (C1-C2, C13-C23) as SUPPORTED, noting well-established literature foundation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these theoretical background claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature review claims (C3-C5, C29-C50) as SUPPORTED, noting balanced coverage of prior findings and acknowledgment of inconsistencies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature summary claims.

OpenEval evaluates citations linking dopamine to working memory updating and maintenance-updating trade-offs (C24-C28) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and well-established empirical support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature claims.
